claim: In the matching retail DLL, Ring.mGetOctagonInSideCrossLine (0x060050FB) has parameters x, y, rp, pb2 and out/ref isp and an exact 538-byte body. It first stores Vector2.zero into isp, allocates two Vector2[2] arrays, stores raw scalar 10.666666030883789, and sets the first moving-segment point to new Vector2(x,y). It subtracts 2 from raw pb2 and switches over exactly four targets, so only pb2 values 2,3,4,5 continue and every other value returns false. For pb2=2 the second moving point is start+(-s,+s) and the comparison edge is (rp.x1,rp.y2)->(rp.x2,rp.y1); pb2=3 uses start+(+s,+s) and (rp.x3,rp.y1)->(rp.x4,rp.y2); pb2=4 uses start+(-s,-s) and (rp.x2,rp.y4)->(rp.x1,rp.y3); pb2=5 uses start+(+s,-s) and (rp.x4,rp.y3)->(rp.x3,rp.y4). All four paths converge by calling Misc.IsIntersect_Segment(out isp, moving[0], moving[1], edge[0], edge[1]) and returning its Boolean result.
